title: Top 6 Responsive (RFPIO) Alternatives and Competitors in 2026: AI-Native and Library-Based
summary: Compare the top 6 Responsive (RFPIO) alternatives and competitors in 2026, from AI-native platforms like Inventive AI to library-based suites. Features, pricing, and ratings.
body_markdown:
‍ *“Responsive is now considered a legacy content management solution whose AI capabilities pale in comparison to basic ad-hoc GenAI tools that are homegrown... Do not sign with them longer than one year!! The technology is quickly becoming obsolete in the face of rapid AI evolution.” says a*[Senior Proposal Manager](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews/responsive-formerly-rfpio-review-11546777) *.*


They also say they are stuck paying for three more years of a contract they regret, highlighting the risk of locking into a platform that may not keep pace with AI.[Another G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews/responsive-formerly-rfpio-review-9148018) says Responsive’s recommendation engine relies heavily on keyword matching and struggles with non-standard questionnaires.


So if you’re evaluating Responsive in 2026, the question is: do you still want to maintain a content library, or do you want AI to generate responses from the knowledge your team already has?


We compared 6 Responsive alternatives for 2026 across AI response capabilities, knowledge management, user and pricing models, and verified customer reviews.


For teams prioritizing AI-generated responses from connected, up-to-date knowledge,[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/) is #1 Responsive alternative to consider. Other options take different approaches: AutoRFP.ai and Arphie are AI-native platforms, 1up is designed for lower-volume response workflows, while Qvidian and Ombud retain a more library- and governance-focused model.


## **TL;DR**


- **Three categories:** Responsive alternatives fall into AI-native platforms, lightweight AI questionnaire tools, and library-based enterprise suites. Responsive itself is library-based.
- **Best Responsive alternative overall:** Inventive AI, with live knowledge, conflict detection, and unlimited users from $830/month.
- **Best for project-based pricing:** AutoRFP.ai, from $899/month for 24 projects per year.
- **Best for low volume:** 1up, from $300/month.
- **Best for Word-centric enterprise teams:** Qvidian.

## **AI-native Responsive alternatives**


AI-native platforms generate answers from connected knowledge, so they cut most of the library maintenance Responsive requires.


### 1. Inventive AI


Inventive AI is an AI-native, agentic RFP platform for RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, security questionnaires, and narrative proposals, with humans approving every response. Founded by leaders from Google DeepMind and Stanford AI and backed by Y Combinator, it suits sales, solutions engineering, and presales teams that want better first drafts and no library to maintain.


#### Why Inventive is the best alternative to Responsive (formerly RFPIO)


Teams leave Responsive mainly because of library upkeep, AI layered onto a legacy Q&A system, and seat-based pricing that limits who can contribute.


Responsive holds[4.5/5 on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews) (1,312 reviews), and[4.5/5 on Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/reviews/) (190 reviews) and users praise its collaboration tools and ease of use, but points below are recurring complaints from a subset of reviewers.


##### 1. Search and auto-fill that struggle with non-standard questions


Several reviewers find Responsive's search and answer recommendations unreliable when a question does not match past wording.


- **What reviewers report:** A[Mid market customer](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews/responsive-formerly-rfpio-review-9148018) of Responsive described the recommendation engine as keyword matching that performs poorly on non-standard questionnaires, which made auto-fill close to useless for them. An[enterprise customer](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews/responsive-formerly-rfpio-review-10166709) reported slow performance, crashes, and search that does not surface all keywords in the content.
- **How Inventive AI handles it:** Our AI context engine draws on the RFP document, project instructions, tone and voice, and meeting notes, and selects sources by relevance and recency.


##### 2. AI drafts that still need heavy review


Reviewers report auto-filled and AI-drafted answers that miss the question or contain wrong statements.


- **What reviewers report:** An[enterprise customer](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews/responsive-formerly-rfpio-review-12292511) said drafts sometimes contain wrong statements even when the source content is accurate. A[Lead underwriting analyst](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/#Capterra___7140408) mentioned auto-responses sometimes do not answer the question being asked.
- **How Inventive AI handles it:** Drafts are grounded in connected company knowledge with source citations, and a conflict-detection agent flags outdated or contradictory answers before they reach a buyer.


##### 3. Library upkeep that never ends


Responsive's output depends on a curated answer library, so quality tracks how well the team maintains it.


- **What reviewers report:** A[customer](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/#Capterra___6678515) said AI recommendations improved only as the answer database grew, and[questions without enough past responses](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/#Capterra___6240971) returned nothing. A[proposal manager](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/#Capterra___6678515) said the response database needs constant maintenance. A[Proposal coordinator](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews/responsive-formerly-rfpio-review-11082181) mentions keeping the library updated constantly is a significant maintenance task.[Another user says](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/reviews/#:~:text=Sometimes%20the%20collaboration,to%20double%20check.) , Sometimes the collaboration with guest accounts can be a bit iffy if I need to involve someone who is not on the platform, I don't always know if they've received the question or reviewed it. Contrasting this with a google docs @ tag, where it's easier to see revisions or they can resolve the tag, I often resort to slack to double check.
- **How Inventive AI handles it:** The[knowledge hub](https://www.inventive.ai/features/knowledge-hub) connects to SharePoint, Google Drive, Confluence, Notion, Zendesk, Salesforce, and Slack, and reads documents natively without converting them into Q&A pairs first.


##### 4. Licensing costs and weak value for money


Some reviewers say Responsive's licensing now costs too much to scale across a team.


- **What reviewers report:** A[manager mentioned](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/#Capterra___6629584) the addition of AI as a game changer for their team, yet said the new licensing model does not support scaling without breaking the bank. A[bid manager in a Computer & Network Security company](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/#Capterra___6689478) mentioned Responsive’s licensing costs as a main drawback. A[customer said Responsive](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons&filters%5Bsentiment_snippet%5D=1778186&filters%5Bcomment_answer_values%5D=&order=lowest_rated&utf8=%E2%9C%93#reviews:~:text=They%20now%20moved%20away%20from%20this%20and%20are%20rapidly%20shifting%20to%20a%20model%20of%20nickeling%20and%20diming%20customers%20for%20blocks%20of%2010%20(both%20users%20and%20projects)%2C%20resulting%20in%20exorbitant%20fees%20in%20comparison%20to%20the%20value%20the%20tool%20actually%20offers%20my%20company.) moved from unlimited users and projects to capped blocks of 10, left them with 90 licensed users of whom fewer than a third use it regularly, and advised against contracts longer than one year. Another[mid market customer](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews/responsive-formerly-rfpio-review-10031910) in **Electronic Manufacturing** says that not all features of Responsive are available with the base package, many of them are paid add-ons, so it can be very expensive to utilize all the features on the platform.
- **How Inventive AI handles it:**[Usage-based pricing](https://www.inventive.ai/inventive-ai-pricing) starts at $830/month billed annually with unlimited users, so SMEs, security teams, and sellers can contribute without seat fees.


##### 5. Import, export, and editing friction


Reviewers describe manual workarounds around imports, exports, and in-app editing.


- **What reviewers report:** A[customer](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/#Capterra___6240971) said entered content disappeared at one point, so they saved after every line, and found editing and inserting pictures difficult. A[responsive user](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/reviews/#:~:text=Would%20like%20a%20little%20more%20sophistication%20in%20some%20functions%20such%20as%20excluding%20certain%20items%20permanently%20from%20the%20duplication%20report.%20I%20also%20still%20manually%20load%20excel%20workbooks%20because%20the%20program%20has%20problems%20properly%20sorting%20complicated%20worksheets.) mentioned they still load Excel workbooks manually because complicated worksheets are not sorted correctly. A[proposal manager in financial services](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/reviews/#:~:text=Currently%20the%20export%20funtion%20is%20my%20least%20love%20of%20Reponsive.%20There%20is%20some%20difficulty%20when%20you%20export%20the%20project%20back%20to%20its%20original%20form.%20There%20are%20many%20work%20arounds%20but%20it%20does%20add%20some%20time%20to%20the%20back%20end%20of%20things.) said exporting a project back to its original form takes workarounds.
- **How Inventive AI handles it:** Inventive AI[exports to Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF, and CSV](https://www.inventive.ai/faq/can-ai-rfp-software-export-into-our-branded-word-powerpoint-and-excel-templates-with-formatting-preserved) and returns the buyer's questionnaire in its original format, so an Excel questionnaire comes back as that questionnaire with answers in place.


##### 6. Steep learning curve and heavy setup


- **What reviewers report:** A[G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews/responsive-formerly-rfpio-review-9348753) said onboarding took too long and Responsive’s UI is complex with too many buttons. Another[responsive user](https://www.capterra.com/p/148054/Responsive/reviews/#:~:text=At%20this%20time%2C%20the%20system%20does%20not%20appear%20to%20be%20very%20user%E2%80%91friendly%20for%20our%20company%E2%80%99s%20needs.%20Our%20requirements%20may%20be%20too%20complex%20for%20its%20intended%20use.) said configuring 20+ templates took a substantial time investment and that day-to-day use would likely be slower than working in Word.
- **How Inventive AI handles it:** Druva, Feedzai, Harte Hanks, and HealthHero all moved from Responsive to Inventive AI smoothly. Druva onboarded 120+ sales team members in 3 weeks after switching.


#### **Inventive AI limitations**


- Reporting dashboards are less customizable than some enterprise tools
- No native Jira integration yet
- Some users want better search, notifications, and mobile experience

### 2. AutoRFP.ai


AutoRFP.ai is an AI-native response platform for RFPs, DDQs, and security questionnaires that drafts from approved content and shows sources on each answer, with unlimited users on every plan.


#### **AutoRFP.ai best features**


- **Cited drafts:** Source citations and trust scores on every answer.
- **Exact-format export:** Keeps the buyer's Word or Excel template, including dropdowns and multi-tab files.
- **Portal automation:** Pulls questions from portals such as Ariba and Jaggaer and pushes answers back.
- **Q&A agent:** Answers questions inside Slack and Microsoft Teams.


#### **AutoRFP.ai limitations**


- Pricing tied to annual project volume can strain teams with unpredictable workloads
- No conflict detection for outdated or contradictory content
- Less suited to highly bespoke responses such as AEC or government contracting


#### AutoRFP.ai pricing


- **Scale:** $899/month (billed annually) for **24 projects/year** , with unlimited users, AI, integrations, and support.
- **Accelerate:** $1,299/month (billed annually) for **50 projects/year** . Enterprise pricing is available for higher project volumes.

### 3. Arphie


Arphie is an AI-native platform for RFPs, security questionnaires, and DDQs that connects to live sources and shows confidence scores and source links on each draft.


#### Arphie best features


- **Live sources:** Connects to Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion, Seismic, and Highspot.
- **Explainable drafts:** Confidence scores, source links, and reasoning for each answer.
- **Duplicate merging:** Identifies and merges duplicate Q&A entries.
- **Security:** SOC 2 Type II, SSO, encryption, and role-based access.


#### Arphie limitations


- Import, export, and formatting need work per user reviews
- Reporting is less mature than established platforms
- No built-in competitive intelligence, and narrative proposal support is limited

## **Lightweight AI Responsive alternatives**


Lightweight AI tools suit small teams with low questionnaire volume that need quick drafts more than enterprise workflow.


### 4. 1up


1up is an AI tool for RFPs and security questionnaires that drafts answers from your website, docs, and knowledge bases, with a browser extension for web-based questionnaires.


#### 1up best features


- **Connected sources:** Pulls from your website, Google Drive, Notion, and Confluence.
- **Browser extension:** Answers inside web portals on Chrome and Edge without copy-pasting.
- **Fast setup:** Free trial and light onboarding for quick proof of value.


#### 1up limitations


- Plans are tied to questionnaire limits, which gets restrictive as volume grows
- Light approvals, governance, and reporting
- Output quality depends heavily on how clean your sources are


#### 1up pricing


- **Free:** Limited plan with 50 AI answers/month.
- **MCP:** $50/month + usage fees ($5 per 100 answers) for teams using their own AI platform.
- **Starter:** $300/month, includes 1 questionnaire automation.
- **Plus:** $900/month, includes 6 questionnaire automations plus Answer Hub, integrations, and browser extension.
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing with unlimited knowledge uploads, dedicated success manager, and enterprise features.

## **Library-based Responsive alternatives**


Library-based suites keep the curated Q&A model Responsive uses and suit teams that want heavy governance, approvals, and admin control. Expect ongoing library upkeep with each.


### **5. Qvidian**


Qvidian, part of Upland Software, is an enterprise proposal platform with governed workflows and deep Microsoft Office integration. It fits large proposal ops teams that build final submissions in Word and Excel.


#### **Qvidian best features**


- **Microsoft integration:** Native Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams support.
- **Content library:** Version control and content expiration for approved responses.
- **Workflows:** Task assignments, approvals, and document parsing.
- **AI Assist:** Generates and revises content inside existing workflows.


#### **Qvidian limitations**


- Interface can feel dated and slow on large projects
- Premium pricing, and SMEs may need paid access to contribute
- No AI-powered conflict detection


#### Qvidian pricing


- Qvidian offers quote-based pricing tailored to your organization's size and requirements and does not list its pricing publicly.
- But, most organizations pay between $15,000 - $25,000/ year for the base license (based on third party review data).


#### Qvidian ratings and reviews


- **G2:**[4.3/5](https://www.g2.com/products/upland-qvidian)

### **6. Ombud**


Ombud is a response platform for RFPs, security questionnaires, proposals, and SOWs, focused on collaboration, content governance, and publishing to branded templates.


#### **Ombud best features**


- **OmMatch:** Suggests answers from a centralized content repository.
- **Collaboration:** Simultaneous editing, task assignments, version history, and approvals.
- **Publishing:** Exports to Word, Excel, PDF, branded templates, and web portals.


#### **Ombud limitations**


- Search and reporting are weaker per user reviews
- Limited native multilingual support
- Pricing is not public


#### Ombud pricing

- They offer quote-based pricing based on team size, deployment, and required features.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is Responsive (formerly RFPIO)?


Responsive is library-based response management software for RFPs, security questionnaires, DDQs, and proposals. RFPIO rebranded as Responsive, so RFPIO, Responsive.io, and Responsive RFP all refer to the same product.


### How much does Responsive cost?


Responsive starts at $5,000/year for 5 users on its Lite plan. Higher tiers are custom quoted on users, features, and add-ons. Our Responsive pricing, features, and reviews guide covers the tiers.


### Is Responsive a good fit for a small sales team?


Usually not. Responsive is built for proposal ops at scale, and seat-based pricing plus library upkeep add overhead a small team rarely needs. Small teams often fit better with Inventive AI or 1up for very low volume.


### Which Responsive alternative reduces RFP editing time the most?


AI-native platforms reduce editing time most because they draft from current sources with citations. In a side-by-side test, RadAI got 2X more usable responses from Inventive AI than from Responsive.


### What is the best Responsive alternative for enterprise RFP teams?


Inventive AI suits enterprise teams that want AI-native drafting with unlimited users, and it is used by Druva, Ripple, and Cushman & Wakefield.


### Does Responsive have an API?


Yes. Responsive offers 75+ APIs and about 30 native integrations, mostly for workflow tools. Its data integrations for pulling knowledge from source systems are newer and more limited.


### Is Responsive now a revenue orchestration platform?


Responsive has broadened its positioning beyond RFPs toward strategic response management across sales content. Its core product is still the Q&A content library.


### Can I move my Responsive library to another tool?


Yes. Most platforms import Q&A libraries, templates, and past proposals. With Inventive AI, you can also connect your source documents directly, so the library does not need to be rebuilt first.


### Is there a Responsive alternative with regional data residency?


Inventive AI is a highly secure, genAI-first alternative to Responsive for automating RFPs, RFIs, and security questionnaires. We offer enterprise-grade data isolation and strict privacy protections.
